business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1, Business)
business_model.claim: Dell Technologies sells technology solutions spanning client devices and peripherals to infrastructure solutions across servers, networking, and storage, to customers in over 170 countries.
quotes: Dell Technologies is a leader in the global technology industry focused on providing broad and innovative technology solutions for the data and artificial intelligence ("AI") era. These solutions range from client devices and peripherals to infrastructure solutions across servers, networking, and storage to meet the evolving needs of our customers and drive better business outcomes.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1 and 10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: Dell operates two reportable segments: Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) and Client Solutions Group (CSG); VMware Resale and other divested businesses are reported in Corporate and other and are not reportable segments.
quotes: We are organized into two business units which are also our reportable segments: Infrastructure Solutions Group and Client Solutions Group.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1 and 10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: ISG's major product categories are AI-optimized servers, traditional servers and networking, and storage; CSG's major product categories are commercial and consumer PCs, peripherals, and services.
quotes: As a result, our major product categories within ISG are our AI-optimized servers offerings, traditional servers and networking offerings, and storage offerings.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (8-K earnings release and 10-Q income statement)
business_model.claim: In Q2 FY27, ISG generated $31,782 (table in millions) in net revenue (up 89% year over year) and CSG generated $15,034 (table in millions) (up 20% year over year), for a consolidated total of $46,971 (table in millions) (up 58% year over year).
quotes: Record revenue of $47.0 billion, up 58% year over year

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1, Dell Payment Solutions section)
business_model.claim: Dell Financial Services (DFS) originated $11.9 billion in customer receivables in Fiscal 2026 and maintained a $14.3 billion global financing receivables portfolio as of January 30, 2026, supporting customers who pay over time via leases, loans, subscriptions, and as-a-Service models.
quotes: DFS funded $11.9 billion of originations in Fiscal 2026 and as of January 30, 2026 maintains a $14.3 billion global portfolio of financing receivables with a strong credit quality.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (8-K earnings release, Q2 FY27)
business_model.claim: Demand for AI-optimized servers is the primary revenue growth driver: in Q2 FY27 Dell booked a record $60.9 billion in AI server orders, recognized a record $16.4 billion in AI server revenue, and exited the quarter with a record $95 billion backlog.
quotes: That's clearest in our AI server business where we booked a record $60.9 billion in orders, recognized a record $16.4 billion in revenue and exited the quarter with a record $95 billion backlog.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-Q MD&A and 10-K MD&A)
business_model.claim: Technology refresh in data centers (driving traditional server and networking demand) and the PC refresh cycle (driving commercial client demand) are secondary revenue growth drivers alongside AI server demand.
quotes: Within our ISG business, we continue to see customers modernize and consolidate their data centers as more customers transition to next-generation products and expand capacity to support growing workloads, which has resulted in significant demand within our traditional servers and networking offerings and our storage offerings. Additionally, within our CSG business, the PC refresh cycle is underway as customers continue to upgrade their devices, which has contributed to significant demand for our commercial offerings.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-Q MD&A, Business Trends and Challenges)
business_model.claim: Component cost inflation, particularly in memory, is a key cost pressure: global supply constraints and substantial inflation in memory component costs are driven by strong and accelerating AI-optimized solution demand and capacity limitations from memory manufacturers.
quotes: Strong and accelerating industry demand for AI‑optimized solutions, together with current limitations in capacity from memory manufacturers, has resulted in global supply constraints and substantial inflation in memory component costs.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-Q MD&A and 10-K MD&A)
business_model.claim: The continuing mix shift toward AI-optimized servers creates anticipated margin rate pressure, even as total gross margin dollars grow.
quotes: We expect margin growth, while balancing anticipated margin rate pressure resulting from a continuing shift in mix towards our AI-optimized servers offerings.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1A, Risk Factors)
business_model.claim: To date, Dell's AI solutions have been purchased primarily by a small number of larger customers and cloud service providers, creating customer concentration and order-timing variability risk.
quotes: While we expect the buyer base for our AI solutions to continue to expand, to date our AI solutions have been purchased primarily by a small number of larger customers and cloud service providers.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1A and 10-K Item 1)
business_model.claim: Sales outside the United States accounted for approximately 45% of consolidated net revenue in Fiscal 2026; approximately 65% of ISG revenue and 60% of CSG revenue are generated in the Americas.
quotes: Sales outside the United States accounted for approximately 45% of our consolidated net revenue for Fiscal 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1, Seasonality)
business_model.claim: Dell's sales exhibit seasonal patterns: ISG storage sales are typically stronger in the fourth fiscal quarter; Americas sales are typically stronger in the second and fourth fiscal quarters; EMEA sales are typically stronger in the fourth fiscal quarter.
quotes: Within ISG, our storage sales are typically stronger in our fourth fiscal quarter. Our sales within the Americas are typically stronger in the second and fourth fiscal quarters, while our sales in EMEA are typically stronger during the fourth fiscal quarter.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1, Research and Development)
business_model.claim: Dell's total R&D expenses were $3.1 billion for both Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025, and $2.8 billion for Fiscal 2024, reflecting investment in software, AI, and next-generation solutions.
quotes: We have a global R&D presence, with total R&D expenses of $3.1 billion for both Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025 and $2.8 billion for Fiscal 2024.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1, Dell Payment Solutions)
business_model.claim: Dell offers customers acquisition choices including utility, subscription, as-a-Service, leases, loans, and immediate pay models, which generate multiyear agreements and recurring revenue streams.
quotes: We offer customers choice in how they acquire our solutions, including utility, subscription, as-a-Service, leases, loans, and immediate pay models. These options allow our customers to pay upfront or over time, providing them with operational and financial flexibility.

quotes: Strong and accelerating industry demand for AI‑optimized solutions, together with current limitations in capacity from memory manufacturers, has resulted in global supply constraints and substantial inflation in memory component costs.
We anticipate notable inflation for component costs in Fiscal 2027 and continue to monitor the rapidly evolving commodity supply environment

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factors), P3 (MD&A macroeconomic discussion), and P1 (manufacturing locations); the specific tariff impact on Dell's costs is not quantified in the evidence.
risks.claim: Trade protection measures including tariffs imposed by the United States and other countries could increase Dell's manufacturing and component costs, reduce demand, or impede cross-border movement of goods across its global supply chain.
quotes: Trade policies and disputes could result in increased tariffs and other trade restrictions and protectionist measures, which could increase our manufacturing costs, increase prices of and reduce demand for our products, limit our ability to sell to certain customers, hamper our procurement of components or raw materials, or impede or slow the movement of our goods across borders.
